text:
cheng: Heads up — spotted a new CVE impacting a transitive C lib we use in the token cache: CVE-2026-0347. NVD initial entry shows memory corruption -> potential RCE, CVSS 8.1 provisional, EPSS 0.72. link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-0347
maya: thanks. which dependency chain? where is it pulled in?
cheng: appears via python-fastcache -> optional C extension used by our cache worker and the inference prefix cache. pipdeptree shows fastcache==1.3.0 pulled by runtime-cache(>=1.0). grep snippet: `pipdeptree | grep -n fastcache`
maya: runtime-cache is deployed in hosted and dedicated pools. worst-case impact: token leakage or remote crash.
tom: can you paste the EPSS/CVSS source? we need to know exploit observed in the wild or PoC.
cheng: EPSS from mitigations feed, NVD mentions PoC on private repo but no public exploit in the wild yet. CVSS vector: AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H (8.1) provisional.
zoe: assigning temp owner to eng-runtime to run quick repro and inventory. @maya can you take?
maya: on it. first step: enumerate services linking compiled wheel. I’ll run `find . -name "*.so" | xargs ldd` in the monorepo builds and check images.
cve-bot: New ticket created — SEC-2026-402: Fastcache (C extension) initial triage and build validation. Priority: P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/SEC-2026-402
maya: quick triage notes: 1) our hosted runtime uses prebuilt wheel fastcache-1.3.0-cp38-manylinux; 2) dedicated pools run mixed wheels, some older pinned to 1.2.7; 3) private onprem customers may have backports.
cheng: risk calcs: service criticality = high (inference prefix cache touches user prompts), exploitability = medium (no public PoC but low AC & no auth), blast radius = medium (affects cached worker pool only). recommend immediate mitigations: temporary disable C-extension build (fallback to pure-Python), add audit logging on cache hits/misses, and schedule security release.
tom: ETA on fallback test? fallback would require rebuilding wheels and republishing. If we disable C extension at runtime we lose perf (~3-4x slower) but reduces memory-corruption risk.
maya: I'll test fallback locally by setting FASTCACHE_USE_CEXT=0 and run perf smoke.
zoe: also suggest adding a WAF rule to block suspicious payloads to ingestion endpoint until patched. I'll coordinate with edge team.
cheng: decision options: A) Emergency patch (upgrade fastcache to 1.4.2 if upstream fixes exist) + canary rollout to dedicated; B) Disable C ext + monitor + plan patch; C) If PoC appears, full incident declared. My recommendation: B immediate, A if upstream has safe release in 24h.
maya: initial test: fallback works, latency regressed ~3.2x in microbench but tail latency for small prompts still acceptable. I'll open PR to gate fallback via env flag and add canary config.
cve-bot: EPSS updated to 0.84 (later feed).
cheng: action items: - maya: PR for fallback + perf validation (due 3h) - zoe: WAF temporary rule + notify edge (due 1h) - tom: coordinate dedicated canary plan & capacity (due 2h) - cheng: draft customer advisory template for on-prem/private (due EOD)
maya: noted, will attach perf numbers to the ticket.
tom: added dedicated canary run in staging pool, will failover if errors > 0.5%
zoe: edge notified, WAF rule in place (monitoring).
cheng: marking thread as initial-triage. If anyone finds upstream release or PoC ping here. :exclamation:
maya: quick grep across codebase found 4 internal repos linking fastcache C ext: runtime-cache, eval-worker, devtools/benchmark, infra/images. Opening small tickets to pin/replace in each repo.
cheng: great — will update SEC-2026-402 with owners. keep updates short here.
